claim_text: Heat treatment sets nanoplate density and thickness: 9.8 per um and ~28 nm as-grown, ~0.3 per um and ~84 nm after 520 C, ~9.0 per um and ~14 nm after the further 400 C anneal

steps.observation: TEM after annealing: the 520 C / water-quenched specimen retains only one thick dark plate, while the further 400 C anneal restores many thin plates
steps.image_note: both panels at 1 um and g=0002, directly comparable with the as-grown panel (b)

panels.caption_span: TEM images showing the variation in microstructure due to heat treatment specimen in Fig. 1 was annealed further at 400C for 5h
TEM images showing the variation in microstructure due to heat treatment specimen in Fig. 1

steps.observation: Nanoplate count falls 9.8 -> 0.3 -> 9.0 per um and mean thickness rises 28 -> 84 -> 14 nm across as-grown / 520 C / 520->400 C
steps.image_note: blue circles on the left axis (0-12 per um), red squares on the right axis (0-~90 nm); only three heat-treatment states, no error bars; the linked text says the annealed density falls 'below 0.1 per um' but the plotted point reads ~0.3 per um

panels.caption_span: Variation in the number of LPSO nanoplates per 1 m and their average thickness according to heat treatment, measured along [0001] in the TEM. The observation direction is parallel to [1120] in all the Figs. 1
